section_text: Payment system means a system that enables payment to be effected between a payer and a beneficiary, involving clearing, payment or settlement service or all of them, but does not include a stock exchange. Includes systems enabling credit card operations, debit card operations, smart card operations, money transfer operations, or similar operations.

No person other than the Reserve Bank shall commence or operate a payment system except under and in accordance with an authorisation issued by the Reserve Bank under the provisions of this Act. Any person operating without authorisation commits an offence under section 26.
amendment_note: This is the source of RBI's power to regulate Payment Aggregators

section_text: Reserve Bank may, on application in prescribed form, issue authorisation for operating a payment system having regard to — (a) need for proposed payment system in context of overall payment and settlement structure; (b) technical standards and design thereof; (c) manner in which payments are to be made and money/securities/instruments transferred; (d) availability of financial resources of the applicant; (e) adequacy of risk-management procedures; (f) compliance with applicable regulations. RBI may impose net-worth, escrow, governance and other conditions.
amendment_note: Net-worth requirement of Rs. 25 crore for PAs flows from this section + Master Direction

section_text: Reserve Bank may revoke the authorisation issued to a system provider if — (a) system provider fails to comply with conditions of authorisation; (b) system provider carries on the payment system in a manner detrimental or prejudicial to the interest of the public or the financial system; (c) system provider fails to comply with any regulation or direction issued by the Reserve Bank; (d) system provider obtained authorisation by fraud or misrepresentation. Revocation only after show-cause notice and opportunity of hearing.

section_title: Power of RBI to determine standards
section_text: Reserve Bank may, in public interest or for the proper management of payment systems or in the interest of payment and settlement systems in the country, determine by regulations, the standards of any payment system including — (a) duration and manner of maintaining records and documents; (b) operational standards including safety, security and efficiency; (c) standards for capital adequacy and credit risk management; (d) criteria for access to the payment system; (e) area of operation of payment system. This is the basis for all RBI Master Directions on PAs/PGs/PPIs.
amendment_note: Source authority for: Master Direction on PA/PG (2020), PPI Master Direction (2021), UPI framework

section_title: Offences and penalties — operating without authorisation
section_text: Whoever commences or operates a payment system without authorisation shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine which may extend to Rs. 10 lakh, or with both. For continuing offence, additional fine up to Rs. 25,000 per day.
amendment_note: Criminal liability — not just civil penalty. Key risk for entities handling funds without PA licence.

section_text: If Reserve Bank is satisfied that a system provider has — (a) contravened any provision of this Act or any regulation, direction or order made thereunder; or (b) failed to produce documents, returns or information — the Reserve Bank may impose penalty not exceeding Rs. 10 lakh and in case of continuing failure, additional penalty up to Rs. 50,000 per day during which such failure continues. Penalty to be imposed only after reasonable opportunity of being heard.
amendment_note: Civil penalty route — alternative to criminal prosecution under s.26

section_text: Reserve Bank may by notification make regulations for — (a) form and manner of application for authorisation; (b) standards for payment systems; (c) net worth requirements; (d) governance standards; (e) customer protection and grievance redressal; (f) data storage and localisation requirements; (g) outsourcing standards; (h) any other matter which is required to be or may be specified by regulations. All Master Directions (PA/PG, PPI, UPI, etc.) derive authority from this section.
amendment_note: The constitutional basis for ALL RBI fintech regulation — PA licensing, PPI rules, UPI framework
